investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a ready state, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent from the check result.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. The scheduler reports 0/6 nodes available: 2 with insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm quota and 4 that do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for ~148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing all contract assertions. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM provisioning layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the two affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are categorically excluded by the pod's affinity/selector, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or stale, the effective capacity ceiling is lower than the cluster's total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity.

Tertiary — resource leak or stuck VMs: previously created remote agent VMs may not have been cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that should have been released. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is intended to handle cleanup, but a prior failed or interrupted run could have left VMs allocated.

Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have been provisioned with a VM limit that is too low for the current eval and workload concurrency, requiring a node pool scale-out or quota increase.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a ready state, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent from the check result.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. The scheduler reports 0/6 nodes available: 2 with insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm quota and 4 that do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for ~148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing all contract assertions. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM provisioning layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata.peerpods.io/vm pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata peerpods resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) is identical across all three sibling checks, confirming the failure is at the VM-slot scheduling layer, not in the eval runner logic or the expected-output contract definition. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918 calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers the kata peerpods pod creation; that pod was stuck unscheduled for ~145–148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and a full contract gap.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' — pod stuck unscheduled for 145s before eval timeout.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=151527, status=fail, endedAt=2026-06-20T16:50:07.795Z — eval ran to near-timeout before failing.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no agent was ever created, so no orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message was captured.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, consistent with the agent pod never starting.
sibling.remote-agent-create: same scheduler error, pod stuck 148s, latencyMs=151241 — the creation step itself failed first.
sibling.remote-agent-state: same scheduler error, pod stuck 146s, latencyMs=151445 — state polling also failed because no agent was ever created.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which is the call that triggers the kata peerpods pod; failure here prevents all downstream evidence collection.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270: contract at line 268 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, message — none present because pod scheduling failed upstream.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes are fully consumed by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero capacity for new eval pods. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free slots.

[Likely secondary] The 4 remaining nodes do not carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource or do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, so the schedulable node pool is structurally limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster capacity.
[Possible] A surge in concurrent remote-agent provisioning requests (from users, other evals, or background jobs) consumed all available VM slots before the eval pods could be scheduled.

[Possible but unconfirmed] A node carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity may have become NotReady or cordoned between runs, reducing effective capacity from a previously higher baseline. No historical run data is available to confirm a regression (verifierContext.history.previousRunCount=0).
